at male.explanation: "At male" means "to paint". To say you paint a wall a color, name the color after the wall: "Han maler væggen hvid" (He paints the wall white). To say you paint a picture, say: "Hun maler et billede" (She paints a picture). To draw with a pencil, use "at tegne" (to draw): "Jeg tegner en hund" (I draw a dog).

sentence.da: Vi vil **male** huset gult.
sentence.en: We want to paint the house yellow.

at mangle.explanation: "At mangle" means "to lack". To say you do not have something you need, say: "Jeg mangler en pen" (I am missing a pen). To say something is missing, start with "der" (there): "Der mangler en stol" (A chair is missing).

sentence.da: Børn må ikke **mangle** mad og tøj.
sentence.en: Children must not lack food and clothes.

at manipulere.explanation: "At manipulere" means "to manipulate". To say someone changes numbers on purpose, say: "at manipulere tal" (to manipulate numbers).

sentence.da: Reklamer kan **manipulere** børn til at ønske sig legetøj.
sentence.en: Ads can manipulate children into wanting toys.

at markere.explanation: "At markere" means "to mark". To say you highlight text so it stands out, say: "Jeg markerer teksten" (I mark the text). To say you recognise an occasion, say: "Vi markerer fødselsdagen med kage" (We mark the birthday with cake).

sentence.da: Du skal **markere** det vigtigste med en gul tusch.
sentence.en: You must mark the most important part with a yellow marker.

at mase.explanation: "At mase" means "to squeeze or push". To say you force your way through a crowd, add "sig igennem" (yourself through): "Han masede sig igennem mængden" (He pushed his way through the crowd).

sentence.da: Folk begyndte at **mase**, da dørene åbnede.
sentence.en: People began to push when the doors opened.

at massere.explanation: "At massere" means "to massage". To say whose body part you massage, put the body part after the verb: "Hun masserer min ryg" (She massages my back).

sentence.da: Han kan **massere** mine skuldre, når de gør ondt.
sentence.en: He can massage my shoulders when they hurt.

at meddele.explanation: "At meddele" means "to announce or inform". To say what you announce, put "at" (that) after it: "Vi meddeler, at kontoret er lukket" (We announce that the office is closed).

sentence.da: Banken vil **meddele** kunderne de nye priser i morgen.
sentence.en: The bank will inform the customers of the new prices tomorrow.

at medføre.explanation: "At medføre" means "to lead to or result in". It is built from "med" (with) and "at føre" (to lead). To say what a cause brings about, put the result after the verb: "Regnen medfører oversvømmelser" (The rain leads to floods).

forms.en: it has led to / resulted in

sentence.da: Det nye system kan **medføre** store besparelser for firmaet.
sentence.en: The new system can lead to big savings for the company.

at meditere.explanation: "At meditere" means "to meditate". To say you meditate at a fixed time, add the time after the verb: "Jeg mediterer hver morgen" (I meditate every morning).

sentence.da: Hun vil **meditere** i stilhed for at slappe af.
sentence.en: She wants to meditate in silence to relax.

at medvirke.explanation: "At medvirke" means "to contribute or take part". To say what you take part in, use "i" (in) after the verb: "at medvirke i en undersøgelse" (to take part in a study).

sentence.da: Flere kendte skuespillere vil **medvirke** i filmen.
sentence.en: Several famous actors will take part in the film.

at melde.explanation: "At melde" means "to report or announce". To say you tell someone that you will not join in, add "fra" (off): "Hun meldte fra til turen" (She said she would not join the trip). To say you put your name down, add "sig til" (yourself for): "Jeg melder mig til kurset" (I sign up for the course).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **melde** mig syg på arbejdet i morgen.
sentence.en: I have to call in sick at work tomorrow.

at melde afbud.explanation: "At melde afbud" means "to cancel your attendance". To say you told the host you could not come, add "til" (to) and the event: "Han meldte afbud til festen" (He canceled his attendance at the party). To say the event itself is canceled, use "at aflyse" (to cancel): "Festen blev aflyst" (The party was canceled).

sentence.da: Jeg må desværre **melde afbud** til mødet.
sentence.en: Unfortunately, I have to tell them I cannot come to the meeting.

at melde sig.explanation: "At melde sig" means "to sign up or volunteer". When you put your name on a list, it means "to sign up": "Jeg melder mig på listen" (I put my name on the list). When you offer to do a job, it means "to volunteer": "Hvem vil melde sig?" (Who will volunteer?)

sentence.da: Man kan **melde sig** på listen ved døren.
sentence.en: You can sign up on the list by the door.

at melde sig syg.explanation: "At melde sig syg" means "to call in sick". It is built from "at melde sig" (to report yourself) and "syg" (sick). To say only how you feel, without telling anyone, use "Jeg er syg" (I am sick).

sentence.da: Han har feber og må **melde sig syg**.
sentence.en: He has a fever and has to call in sick.

at melde sig til.explanation: "At melde sig til" means "to sign up for". To ask where people can sign up, you can leave out the thing you sign up for: "Hvor kan man melde sig til?" (Where can you sign up?)

sentence.da: Hun vil **melde sig til** fodboldholdet i år.
sentence.en: She wants to sign up for the soccer team this year.

at melde til politiet.explanation: "At melde til politiet" means "to report to the police". To say what you report, put it between "melde" and "til": "Han meldte tyveriet til politiet" (He reported the theft to the police).

forms.en: I have reported to the police

sentence.da: Når man bliver bestjålet, bør man **melde til politiet**.
sentence.en: When something is stolen from you, you should report it to the police.

at mene.explanation: "At mene" means "to mean or think". To give your opinion, put "at" (that) after it: "Jeg mener, at du har ret" (I think you are right). To ask for someone's opinion: "Hvad mener du?" (What do you mean?) To say how something seems to you, use "at synes" (to think): "Jeg synes, at maden er god" (I think the food is good). To ask what a word means, use "at betyde" (to mean): "Hvad betyder ordet?" (What does the word mean?)

sentence.da: Du må gerne **mene** noget andet.
sentence.en: You are welcome to think something else.

at mime.explanation: "At mime" means "to mime". To ask someone to act out a word without speaking, say: "Kan du mime ordet?" (Can you mime the word?)

sentence.da: Hun kan **mime** en hel historie uden at sige noget.
sentence.en: She can mime a whole story without saying anything.

at minde om.explanation: "At minde om" means "to remind of". When a person brings another person to your mind, put "mig" (me) before "om": "Du minder mig om min bror" (You remind me of my brother). To remind someone to do something, add "at" (to) and the action: "Jeg minder dig om at ringe" (I remind you to call). When one thing looks like another, it means "to resemble": "Hotellet minder om et slot" (The hotel resembles a castle).

sentence.da: Den sang kan **minde om** sommeren.
sentence.en: That song can remind you of summer.

at mindes.explanation: "At mindes" means "to remember or commemorate". To say you think back on a person from the past, use the person after it: "Vi mindes vores bedstefar" (We remember our grandfather). To remember a fact, use "at huske" (to remember): "Jeg husker dit navn" (I remember your name).

sentence.da: Vi vil **mindes** dem, der døde i krigen.
sentence.en: We want to remember those who died in the war.

at mindske.explanation: "At mindske" means "to reduce". To say you lower a danger, use "risikoen" (the risk): "Vi vil mindske risikoen for ulykker" (We want to reduce the risk of accidents).

sentence.da: Man kan **mindske** forbruget ved at slukke lyset.
sentence.en: You can reduce consumption by turning off the light.

at misforstå.explanation: "At misforstå" means "to misunderstand". It is built from "mis" (wrongly) and "at forstå" (to understand). The same "mis" starts "at misbruge" (to misuse). To ask someone not to take your words the wrong way, say: "Misforstå mig ikke" (Do not misunderstand me).

sentence.da: Jeg kan nemt **misforstå** dig på telefonen.
sentence.en: I can easily misunderstand you on the phone.

at mislykkes.explanation: "At mislykkes" means "to fail". To say an attempt did not work out, use the attempt as the subject: "Forsøget mislykkedes" (The attempt failed). To say a student failed an exam, use "at dumpe" (to flunk): "Hun dumpede til eksamen" (She flunked the exam).

sentence.da: Hvis planen **mislykkes**, må vi prøve noget andet.
sentence.en: If the plan fails, we must try something else.

at misse.explanation: "At misse" means "to miss", as in not catching a train or bus. For example, "Vi missede toget" (We missed the train). To miss a person, use "at savne" (to miss): "Jeg savner dig" (I miss you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **misse** bussen i morgen tidlig.
sentence.en: I don't want to miss the bus tomorrow morning.

at miste.explanation: "At miste" means "to lose (something)". To say you lose an object, use the object after it: "Jeg mistede min nøgle" (I lost my key). To say a person dies, use the person after it: "Hun mistede sin bedstefar" (She lost her grandfather). To say you lose a game, use "at tabe" (to lose): "Vi tabte kampen" (We lost the match).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **miste** min telefon igen.
sentence.en: I don't want to lose my phone again.

at mistænke.explanation: "At mistænke" means "to suspect". To say what you suspect is going on, use "at" (that) after it: "Jeg mistænker, at han lyver" (I suspect that he is lying).

sentence.da: Politiet kan **mistænke** en nabo for tyveriet.
sentence.en: The police may suspect a neighbor of the theft.

at mjave.explanation: "At mjave" means "to meow". To say a cat purrs, use "at spinde" (to purr): "Katten spinder" (The cat purrs).

sentence.da: Jeg kan høre katten **mjave** udenfor.
sentence.en: I can hear the cat meow outside.

at modarbejde.explanation: "At modarbejde" means "to counteract". It is built from "mod" (against) and "at arbejde" (to work). The same "mod" starts "at modsige" (to contradict).

sentence.da: Nogle kolleger prøver at **modarbejde** den nye chef.
sentence.en: Some colleagues try to work against the new boss.

at modbevise.explanation: "At modbevise" means "to disprove". It is built from "mod" (against) and "at bevise" (to prove). To say what you disprove, put it after the verb: "at modbevise en teori" (to disprove a theory).

sentence.da: Et godt alibi kan **modbevise**, at man var der.
sentence.en: A good alibi can disprove that you were there.

at moderere.explanation: "At moderere" means "to moderate". To say someone runs a debate, put the debate after the verb: "Hun modererer debatten" (She moderates the debate).

sentence.da: Du bør **moderere** dit sprog, når børnene hører på.
sentence.en: You should tone down your language when the children are listening.

at modsige.explanation: "At modsige" means "to contradict". It is built from "mod" (against) and "at sige" (to say). To say one fact does not agree with another, say: "Det modsiger, hvad du sagde før" (That contradicts what you said before). To say you contradict yourself, add "sig selv" (yourself): "Du modsiger dig selv" (You contradict yourself).

sentence.da: Optagelserne kan **modsige** vidnets forklaring.
sentence.en: The recordings can contradict the witness's statement.

at modstille.explanation: "At modstille" means "to contrast". It is built from "mod" (against) and "at stille" (to put). To say you set two things side by side, put both after the verb: "at modstille by og land" (to contrast city and country).

sentence.da: Artiklen vil **modstille** to meget forskellige syn på skolen.
sentence.en: The article wants to contrast two very different views of the school.

at modstå.explanation: "At modstå" means "to resist". It is built from "mod" (against) and "at stå" (to stand). To say a building holds up against a force, put the force after the verb: "Huset kan modstå stormen" (The house can withstand the storm).

sentence.da: Jeg kan aldrig **modstå** en frisk kage.
sentence.en: I can never resist a fresh cake.

at modtage.explanation: "At modtage" means "to receive". To say you got an email, say: "Jeg har modtaget din mail" (I have received your email). To say you got a gift in plain words, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik en gave" (I got a gift).

sentence.da: Vi skal **modtage** en pakke i morgen.
sentence.en: We are going to receive a package tomorrow.

at modvirke.explanation: "At modvirke" means "to counteract". To say something weakens a problem, put the problem after the verb: "Motion kan modvirke stress" (Exercise can counteract stress). To say a person works against your plans, use "at modarbejde" (to work against): "Han modarbejder mine planer" (He works against my plans).

sentence.da: Sund mad kan **modvirke** træthed hen på dagen.
sentence.en: Healthy food can counteract tiredness later in the day.

at more sig.explanation: "At more sig" means "to have fun". The small word "sig" (oneself) must be used with it and changes with the person. To talk about "vi" (we), use "os": "Vi morer os" (We are having fun). To ask someone if they had fun, say: "Morede du dig?" (Did you have fun?)

sentence.da: Børnene skal **more sig** til festen.
sentence.en: The children are going to have fun at the party.

at motionere.explanation: "At motionere" means "to exercise", as in working out your body. To say how often you work out, add the time after the verb: "Jeg motionerer tre gange om ugen" (I exercise three times a week). The noun is "motion" (exercise). For example, "Motion er godt for dig" (Exercise is good for you).

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at jeg skal **motionere** mere.
sentence.en: The doctor says that I should exercise more.

at motivere.explanation: "At motivere" means "to motivate". To say who you motivate, put the person after the verb: "Læreren motiverer eleverne" (The teacher motivates the students). To say you motivate yourself, add "mig selv" (myself): "Jeg motiverer mig selv" (I motivate myself).

sentence.da: En god leder kan **motivere** hele holdet.
sentence.en: A good leader can motivate the whole team.

at mumle.explanation: "At mumle" means "to mumble". To say what someone mumbled, put the words after the verb: "Han mumlede noget, jeg ikke forstod" (He mumbled something I did not understand).

sentence.da: Han begyndte at **mumle**, så ingen kunne forstå ham.
sentence.en: He started to mumble, so no one could understand him.

at myrde.explanation: "At myrde" means "to murder". To say someone is killed, even by accident, use "at dræbe" (to kill): "Uheldet dræbte to personer" (The accident killed two people).

sentence.da: Han blev dømt for at **myrde** sin nabo.
sentence.en: He was convicted of murdering his neighbor.

at måle.explanation: "At måle" means "to measure". To say a doctor takes your temperature, Danish uses "måle" (to measure): "Lægen måler min temperatur" (The doctor is taking my temperature).

sentence.da: Man kan **måle** længden med en lineal.
sentence.en: You can measure the length with a ruler.

at måtte.explanation: "At måtte" means "may or must". When you ask for permission, it means "may": "Må jeg gå?" (May I go?) When you say you have to do something, it means "must": "Jeg må gå nu" (I have to go now). To forbid something, add "ikke" (not): "Du må ikke løbe her" (You must not run here). Put the next verb right after it, without "at" (to): "Jeg må gå" (I have to go).

forms.en: I was allowed to / had to

sentence.da: Vi kommer til at **måtte** vente en time.
sentence.en: We will have to wait an hour.

at mærke.explanation: "At mærke" means "to feel or notice". To say you feel something physical, put it after the verb: "Jeg mærker regnen" (I feel the rain). To say you did not notice something, add "ikke" (not): "Han mærkede ikke noget" (He did not notice anything).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **mærke** vinden i mit ansigt.
sentence.en: I can feel the wind on my face.

at mætte.explanation: "At mætte" means "to fill (up) or satisfy". To say food filled people up, put the people after the verb: "Maden mættede os alle" (The food filled us all up).

sentence.da: En stor portion pasta kan **mætte** hele familien.
sentence.en: A large portion of pasta can fill up the whole family.

at møde op.explanation: "At møde op" means "to show up". It is built from "at møde" (to meet) and "op" (up). To say someone came on time, add the time: "Han mødte op til tiden" (He showed up on time). To say someone did not come, add "ikke" (not): "Hun mødte ikke op" (She did not show up).

sentence.da: Alle skal **møde op** klokken otte.
sentence.en: Everyone has to show up at eight o'clock.

at mødes.explanation: "At mødes" means "to meet (each other)". To say people meet each other, say: "Vi mødes i morgen" (We meet tomorrow). To say you meet one person, leave off the "s" and use "at møde" (to meet): "Jeg møder Anna" (I meet Anna).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **mødes** på cafeen i morgen.
sentence.en: We would like to meet at the cafe tomorrow.

en madallergi.explanation: "En madallergi" means "a food allergy". The first part, "mad" (food), also starts "madpakke" (a packed lunch).

sentence.da: Min søn har en **madallergi** og kan ikke spise æg.
sentence.en: My son has a food allergy and cannot eat eggs.

en madanmelder.explanation: "En madanmelder" means "a food critic". The second part, "anmelder" (critic), also ends "en filmanmelder" (a film critic).

sentence.da: Vores **madanmelder** gav restauranten fem stjerner i avisen.
sentence.en: Our food critic gave the restaurant five stars in the paper.

en madding.explanation: "En madding" means "bait". To say fish take the bait, use "bide på" (to bite on): "Fisken bider på maddingen" (The fish bites the bait).

sentence.da: Ormen er en god **madding**, når man fisker efter ørred.
sentence.en: The worm is good bait when you fish for trout.

en madkasse.explanation: "En madkasse" means "a lunch box". It is built from "mad" (food) and "en kasse" (a box). To say what is inside, use "i" (in): "Der er et æble i min madkasse" (There is an apple in my lunch box).

sentence.da: Min søn tager sin **madkasse** med i skole.
sentence.en: My son takes his lunch box to school.

en madkultur.explanation: "En madkultur" means "a food culture". To say whose food culture, put the nationality before it: "dansk madkultur" (Danish food culture).

sentence.da: I Danmark er rugbrød en vigtig del af vores **madkultur**.
sentence.en: In Denmark rye bread is an important part of our food culture.

en madordning.explanation: "En madordning" means "a meal program". It is built from "mad" (food) and "en ordning" (an arrangement).

sentence.da: Børnehaven har en **madordning** med frokost hver dag.
sentence.en: The kindergarten has a meal program with lunch every day.

en madpakke.explanation: "En madpakke" means "a packed lunch". It is built from "mad" (food) and "en pakke" (a package). To remind someone to take theirs, say: "Husk din madpakke" (Remember your packed lunch).

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **madpakke** med på arbejde.
sentence.en: I take my packed lunch to work.

en madplan.explanation: "En madplan" means "a meal plan". It is built from "mad" (food) and "en plan" (a plan). To say the plan covers a period, use "for" (for): "en madplan for ugen" (a meal plan for the week).

sentence.da: Vi laver en **madplan** hver søndag og køber ind til hele ugen.
sentence.en: We make a meal plan every Sunday and shop for the whole week.

en madras.explanation: "En madras" means "a mattress". The "s" doubles when an ending is added, as in "madrassen" (the mattress).

sentence.da: Jeg sover bedre på en blød **madras**.
sentence.en: I sleep better on a soft mattress.

en madrest.explanation: "En madrest" means "a food scrap". It is built from "mad" (food) and "rest" (remainder).

sentence.da: Der er kun en lille **madrest** tilbage på tallerkenen.
sentence.en: There is only a small food scrap left on the plate.

en madvare.explanation: "En madvare" means "a food product". To say drinks, use "drikkevarer" (drinks): "Butikken sælger madvarer og drikkevarer" (The shop sells food products and drinks).

sentence.da: Mælk er en **madvare**, og den skal stå i køleskabet.
sentence.en: Milk is a food product, and it has to be kept in the fridge.

en madvogn.explanation: "En madvogn" means "a food truck". The second part, "vogn" (cart), also ends "en barnevogn" (a baby carriage).

sentence.da: Ved festivalen står der en **madvogn** med burgere og pommes frites.
sentence.en: At the festival there is a food truck with burgers and fries.

en mafia.explanation: "En mafia" means "a mafia". To say someone belongs to it, use "med i" (in): "Han er med i mafiaen" (He is in the mafia).

sentence.da: Filmen handler om en **mafia** i New York.
sentence.en: The movie is about a mafia in New York.

en magt.explanation: "En magt" means "a power", as in the power to decide things. To say the electric power is out, use "strøm" (electricity): "Strømmen er gået" (The power is out).

sentence.da: Politikere har **magt**, fordi vi stemmer på dem.
sentence.en: Politicians have power because we vote for them.

en mail.explanation: "En mail" means "an email". It is a shorter way to write "en e-mail" (an email). To say you got one, say: "Jeg fik en mail fra min chef" (I got an email from my boss).

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig en **mail** i dag.
sentence.en: I am sending you an email today.

en majestæt.explanation: "En majestæt" means "a majesty". To speak to a king or queen directly, say: "Deres Majestæt" (Your Majesty).

sentence.da: Man siger **majestæt**, når man taler til kongen.
sentence.en: You say Majesty when you talk to the king.

en major.explanation: "En major" means "a major", as in the military rank. To say something is important, use "vigtig" (important): "Det er et vigtigt møde" (It is an important meeting).

sentence.da: En **major** er højere i rang end en kaptajn.
sentence.en: A major is higher in rank than a captain.

en makrel.explanation: "En makrel" means "a mackerel". In Denmark, you can buy it in a can as "makrel i tomat" (mackerel in tomato sauce).

sentence.da: En **makrel** har striber på ryggen og lever i havet.
sentence.en: A mackerel has stripes on its back and lives in the sea.

en maler.explanation: "En maler" means "a painter". To talk about someone who makes art, say: "Maleren udstiller på museet" (The painter is showing work at the museum). To talk about someone who paints walls, say: "Maleren skal male stuen" (The painter is going to paint the living room).

sentence.da: Min bror er **maler** og maler huse.
sentence.en: My brother is a painter and paints houses.

en manager.explanation: "En manager" means "a manager". It is borrowed from English. To talk about the boss at an ordinary workplace, use "en chef" (a boss): "Min chef er sød" (My boss is nice).

sentence.da: Sangerens **manager** ordner alle koncerter og aftaler.
sentence.en: The singer's manager arranges all the concerts and deals.

en manchetknap.explanation: "En manchetknap" means "a cufflink". It is built from "manchet" (cuff) and "en knap" (a button). To say you are wearing them, say: "Han har manchetknapper på" (He is wearing cufflinks).

sentence.da: Han lukker skjortens ærme med en **manchetknap** af sølv.
sentence.en: He closes the shirt sleeve with a silver cufflink.

en mand.explanation: "En mand" means "a man or a husband". The plural "mænd" (men) changes the vowel. For example, "to mænd" (two men).

sentence.da: Min **mand** og jeg har to børn.
sentence.en: My husband and I have two children.

en mandel.explanation: "En mandel" means "an almond". To talk about the body part in your throat, it means "tonsil": "Han fik fjernet mandlerne" (He had his tonsils removed).

sentence.da: Marcipan er lavet af **mandel** og sukker.
sentence.en: Marzipan is made of almond and sugar.

en mangel.explanation: "En mangel" means "a shortage". To say what there is too little of, use "på" (of) after it: "mangel på vand" (a shortage of water). To say a bought item is faulty, it means "defect": "Varen har en mangel" (The item has a defect).

sentence.da: Der er **mangel** på sygeplejersker i mange lande.
sentence.en: There is a shortage of nurses in many countries.

en mango.explanation: "En mango" means "a mango". The plural is "mangoer" (mangoes). For example, "to mangoer" (two mangoes).

sentence.da: En **mango** er gul og blød indeni.
sentence.en: A mango is yellow and soft inside.

en manke.explanation: "En manke" means "a mane". To talk about a lion, say: "Løven har en stor manke" (The lion has a big mane).

sentence.da: Hesten har en lang, sort **manke** på halsen.
sentence.en: The horse has a long, black mane on its neck.

en mappe.explanation: "En mappe" means "a folder". To say you make a new one, use "at oprette" (to create): "at oprette en mappe" (to create a folder).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger alle billederne i en ny **mappe**.
sentence.en: I put all the pictures in a new folder.

en mariehøne.explanation: "En mariehøne" means "a ladybug". Literally, it is "Mary's hen", from "en høne" (a hen). The plural is "mariehøns" (ladybugs). For example, "to mariehøns" (two ladybugs).

sentence.da: En rød **mariehøne** har sorte prikker på ryggen.
sentence.en: A red ladybug has black dots on its back.

en mark.explanation: "En mark" means "a field", as in a farmer's land. Do not mix it up with "et marked" (a market). For example, "Vi køber frugt på et marked" (We buy fruit at a market).

sentence.da: Bonden kører en traktor ud på sin **mark**.
sentence.en: The farmer drives a tractor out onto his field.

en markedsandel.explanation: "En markedsandel" means "a market share". It is built from "et marked" (a market) and "en andel" (a share).

sentence.da: Firmaet har en **markedsandel** på tyve procent i Danmark.
sentence.en: The company has a market share of twenty percent in Denmark.

en markedsbod.explanation: "En markedsbod" means "a market stall". It is built from "marked" (market) and "bod" (stall). To talk about a small storage room in an apartment building, use "en bod" (a storage room): "Cyklen står i boden" (The bike is in the storage room).

sentence.da: Jeg køber friske æbler i en **markedsbod**.
sentence.en: I buy fresh apples at a market stall.

en markering.explanation: "En markering" means "a marking or a demonstration". To talk about a painted line on a road, say: "hvide markeringer på vejen" (white markings on the road). To talk about a public show of respect, say: "Vi holdt et minuts stilhed som markering" (We held a minute of silence as a show of respect).

sentence.da: Cykelstien er vist med en hvid **markering** på vejen.
sentence.en: The bike path is shown with a white marking on the road.

en marketingchef.explanation: "En marketingchef" means "a marketing manager". It is built from "marketing" (marketing) and "en chef" (a boss). The same "chef" ends "en økonomichef" (a finance manager).

sentence.da: Vores **marketingchef** planlægger reklamerne til næste år.
sentence.en: Our marketing manager plans the ads for next year.

en mascara.explanation: "En mascara" means "a mascara". To say you put it on, use "at tage ... på" (to put on): "Jeg tager mascara på" (I put on mascara).

sentence.da: Med **mascara** bliver mine øjenvipper mørke.
sentence.en: With mascara my eyelashes get dark.

en maske.explanation: "En maske" means "a mask". To say you put one on, use "at tage ... på" (to put on): "Han tager en maske på" (He puts on a mask).

sentence.da: Lægen har en **maske** over munden.
sentence.en: The doctor has a mask over his mouth.

en maskine.explanation: "En maskine" means "a machine". It is the last part of other words, such as "en vaskemaskine" (a washing machine).

sentence.da: Den nye **maskine** er hurtig, men larmer meget.
sentence.en: The new machine is fast but makes a lot of noise.

en massage.explanation: "En massage" means "a massage". To say you got one, you can leave out "en" after "få" (to get): "Jeg fik massage" (I got a massage).

sentence.da: En time **massage** hjælper, når ryggen er spændt.
sentence.en: An hour of massage helps when the back is tense.

en masse.explanation: "En masse" means "a lot or a mass". To say a lot of something, put the thing right after it, without "af" (of): "en masse penge" (a lot of money).

sentence.da: Der var en **masse** mennesker i byen.
sentence.en: There were a lot of people in town.

en matematiker.explanation: "En matematiker" means "a mathematician". The ending "-iker" names a person in other words. For example, "en fysiker" (a physicist) and "en kemiker" (a chemist).

sentence.da: En **matematiker** bruger tal og logik til at løse svære problemer.
sentence.en: A mathematician uses numbers and logic to solve hard problems.

en mave.explanation: "En mave" means "a stomach". To say your stomach hurts, say: "Jeg har ondt i maven" (My stomach hurts). To talk about the belly on the outside of the body, it also means "belly": "Han klappede sig på maven" (He patted his belly).

sentence.da: Maden går ned i din **mave**.
sentence.en: The food goes down into your stomach.

en mavebøjning.explanation: "En mavebøjning" means "a sit-up". The second part comes from "at bøje" (to bend), as in "en armbøjning" (a push-up).

sentence.da: Man ligger på ryggen og løfter overkroppen i en **mavebøjning**.
sentence.en: You lie on your back and lift your upper body in a sit-up.

en mavepine.explanation: "En mavepine" means "a stomachache". It is built from "mave" (stomach) and "pine" (pain). To say the same thing with "ondt" (pain), say: "Jeg har ondt i maven" (My stomach hurts).

sentence.da: Jeg har **mavepine** og vil ikke spise.
sentence.en: I have a stomachache and don't want to eat.

en mavesæk.explanation: "En mavesæk" means "a stomach (organ)". It is built from "mave" (stomach) and "en sæk" (a bag). To talk about the belly on the outside of the body, use "mave" (belly): "Han har en stor mave" (He has a big belly).

sentence.da: Når du sluger maden, ender den i din **mavesæk**.
sentence.en: When you swallow the food, it ends up in your stomach.

en medalje.explanation: "En medalje" means "a medal". To name the kind, put the metal in front: "en guldmedalje" (a gold medal) and "en sølvmedalje" (a silver medal).

sentence.da: Min datter vandt en **medalje** i svømning.
sentence.en: My daughter won a medal in swimming.

en medarbejder.explanation: "En medarbejder" means "an employee". It is built from "med" (with) and "en arbejder" (a worker). The same "med" means "fellow" in "en medstuderende" (a fellow student) and "en medspiller" (a fellow player).

sentence.da: Vores nye **medarbejder** starter på mandag.
sentence.en: Our new employee starts on Monday.

en medborgerskabsprøve.explanation: "En medborgerskabsprøve" means "a civics test". In Denmark, it is a test about Danish society, history and culture for people from abroad. It is built from "medborgerskab" (citizenship) and "en prøve" (a test).

sentence.da: Hun skal bestå en **medborgerskabsprøve** om dansk historie og samfund.
sentence.en: She must pass a civics test about Danish history and society.

en meddelelse.explanation: "En meddelelse" means "an announcement". It comes from the verb "at meddele" (to announce). To talk about a message to a friend, use "en besked" (a message): "Jeg sendte hende en besked" (I sent her a message).

sentence.da: Skolen sendte en **meddelelse** om den nye fridag.
sentence.en: The school sent an announcement about the new day off.

en medisterpølse.explanation: "En medisterpølse" means "a Danish pork sausage". It is built from "medister" (a spiced minced pork mixture) and "en pølse" (a sausage).

sentence.da: Til aftensmad steger vi en **medisterpølse** med kartofler.
sentence.en: For dinner we fry a medister sausage with potatoes.

en meditation.explanation: "En meditation" means "a meditation". The matching verb is "at meditere" (to meditate).

sentence.da: Under en **meditation** sidder man stille og tænker på sin vejrtrækning.
sentence.en: During a meditation you sit still and think about your breathing.

en medspiller.explanation: "En medspiller" means "a teammate". To talk about someone who plays against you, use "en modspiller" (an opponent): "Min modspiller var stærk" (My opponent was strong).

sentence.da: En god **medspiller** hjælper de andre på holdet.
sentence.en: A good teammate helps the others on the team.

en mejetærsker.explanation: "En mejetærsker" means "a combine harvester". It is built from "at meje" (to reap) and "at tærske" (to thresh).

sentence.da: Landmanden bruger en **mejetærsker**, når kornet er modent.
sentence.en: The farmer uses a combine harvester when the grain is ripe.

en mekaniker.explanation: "En mekaniker" means "a mechanic". It is the last part of other job words, such as "en cykelmekaniker" (a bike mechanic).

sentence.da: En **mekaniker** reparerer biler og motorer.
sentence.en: A mechanic repairs cars and engines.

en mellemlanding.explanation: "En mellemlanding" means "a layover". It is built from "mellem" (between) and "en landing" (a landing). The same "mellem" starts "et mellemmåltid" (a snack between meals).

sentence.da: På turen til Thailand har vi en **mellemlanding** i Dubai.
sentence.en: On the trip to Thailand, we have a layover in Dubai.

en melodi.explanation: "En melodi" means "a melody". To say someone hums a tune, use "at nynne" (to hum): "Han nynner en melodi" (He hums a tune).

sentence.da: Jeg kender den smukke **melodi**, men ikke teksten.
sentence.en: I know the beautiful melody, but not the lyrics.

en melon.explanation: "En melon" means "a melon". To name a kind, put the type in front: "en vandmelon" (a watermelon).

sentence.da: En **melon** er stor, rund og sød indeni.
sentence.en: A melon is big, round and sweet inside.

en mening.explanation: "En mening" means "an opinion". To ask what someone thinks, say: "Hvad er din mening?" (What is your opinion?) To say something makes no sense, "mening" means "sense": "Det giver ingen mening" (That makes no sense).

sentence.da: Jeg har en anden **mening** end dig.
sentence.en: I have a different opinion than you.

en meningsmåling.explanation: "En meningsmåling" means "an opinion poll". It is built from "en mening" (an opinion) and "en måling" (a measurement).

sentence.da: Ifølge en ny **meningsmåling** er flere unge utilfredse.
sentence.en: According to a new opinion poll, more young people are unhappy.

en mentor.explanation: "En mentor" means "a mentor". To say someone guides you, say: "Hun er min mentor" (She is my mentor).

sentence.da: En **mentor** hjælper en nyansat med at lære jobbet.
sentence.en: A mentor helps a new employee learn the job.

en menu.explanation: "En menu" means "a menu". To talk about the set meal a restaurant offers on one day, use "dagens menu" (the menu of the day): "Dagens menu er fisk" (The menu of the day is fish).

sentence.da: Vi får en **menu** og vælger mad.
sentence.en: We get a menu and choose food.

en mester.explanation: "En mester" means "a master or champion". To name a master of a craft, put the craft first: "en tømrermester" (a master carpenter).

sentence.da: Min bror er **mester** i skak.
sentence.en: My brother is a chess champion.

en meter.explanation: "En meter" means "a meter". To say how tall something is, use a number before it: "Træet er ti meter højt" (The tree is ten meters tall).

sentence.da: Han er over to **meter** høj.
sentence.en: He is over two meters tall.

en metode.explanation: "En metode" means "a method". To say you use a certain way of working, use "at bruge" (to use): "Jeg bruger en ny metode" (I use a new method).

sentence.da: En **metode** er en bestemt måde at løse en opgave på.
sentence.en: A method is a certain way of solving a task.

en metro.explanation: "En metro" means "a metro". To say how you travel, use "med" (by): "Jeg kører med metroen" (I go by metro). Copenhagen has a metro.

sentence.da: Jeg kører med **metro** under jorden.
sentence.en: I ride the metro underground.

en middag.explanation: "En middag" means "a dinner". When you give the time of day, "middag" also means "noon": "Klokken tolv er det middag" (At twelve o'clock it is noon). For the meal around that time, use "frokost" (lunch): "Vi spiser frokost klokken tolv" (We eat lunch at twelve).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **middag** klokken seks om aftenen.
sentence.en: We eat dinner at six in the evening.

en middagslur.explanation: "En middagslur" means "a nap". It is built from "middag" (midday) and "en lur" (a nap). To say you take a nap, use "at tage" (to take): "Jeg tager en middagslur" (I take a nap).

sentence.da: Små børn tager ofte en **middagslur** efter frokost.
sentence.en: Small children often take a nap after lunch.

en midtergang.explanation: "En midtergang" means "an aisle". It is built from "midt" (middle) and "en gang" (a hallway). The same "gang" is the word for a hallway in a house. For example, "Skoene står i gangen" (The shoes are in the hallway).

sentence.da: Han går ned ad en lang **midtergang** i flyet.
sentence.en: He walks down a long aisle in the plane.

en migræne.explanation: "En migræne" means "a migraine". To name one attack, add "anfald" (attack): "et migræneanfald" (a migraine attack).

sentence.da: Når jeg har **migræne**, kan jeg ikke tåle lys.
sentence.en: When I have a migraine, I cannot stand light.

en mikrobølgeovn.explanation: "En mikrobølgeovn" means "a microwave oven". It is built from "mikro" (micro), "en bølge" (a wave) and "en ovn" (an oven). The shorter word is "en mikroovn" (a microwave). For example, "Jeg varmer maden i mikroovnen" (I warm the food in the microwave).

sentence.da: Man varmer mad op i en **mikrobølgeovn**.
sentence.en: You heat up food in a microwave oven.

en mikrofon.explanation: "En mikrofon" means "a microphone". To tell someone on a video call to unmute, say: "Slå din mikrofon til" (Turn on your microphone).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke høre dig, fordi din **mikrofon** er slukket.
sentence.en: I cannot hear you because your microphone is off.

en mikroovn.explanation: "En mikroovn" means "a microwave". It is a shorter word for "en mikrobølgeovn" (a microwave oven). To say something is inside the microwave, use "i" (in): "Kaffen står i mikroovnen" (The coffee is in the microwave).

sentence.da: Maden bliver varm hurtigt i en **mikroovn**.
sentence.en: The food gets hot fast in a microwave.

en mil.explanation: "En mil" means "a mil". It is an old Danish measure of distance of about 7.5 km, much longer than an English mile. A common phrase is "på mils afstand" (from miles away). For example, "Det kan man se på mils afstand" (You can see that from miles away).

sentence.da: Før i tiden målte man afstand i **mil**.
sentence.en: In the old days, people measured distance in mil.

en milepæl.explanation: "En milepæl" means "a milestone". It is built from "mil" (an old measure of distance) and "en pæl" (a post). To say a project has reached an important point, use "at nå" (to reach): "Vi har nået en milepæl" (We have reached a milestone).

sentence.da: Vores første salg var en **milepæl** for firmaet.
sentence.en: Our first sale was a milestone for the company.

en milkshake.explanation: "En milkshake" means "a milkshake". It comes from the English word "milkshake". To order one, say: "Jeg vil gerne have en jordbærmilkshake" (I would like a strawberry milkshake).

sentence.da: En **milkshake** er lavet af mælk og is.
sentence.en: A milkshake is made of milk and ice cream.

en milliard.explanation: "En milliard" means "a billion". It is a thousand million. For example, "en milliard kroner" (a billion kroner). Do not mix it up with "en billion", which is a million million, so a trillion. For another example, "en billion kroner" (a trillion kroner).

sentence.da: Kina har over en **milliard** mennesker.
sentence.en: China has over a billion people.

en mindehøjtidelighed.explanation: "En mindehøjtidelighed" means "a memorial service". It is built from "et minde" (a memory) and "en højtidelighed" (a ceremony). The same "minde" is in "en mindetale" (a memorial speech).

sentence.da: Efter krigen holdt byen en **mindehøjtidelighed** for de faldne.
sentence.en: After the war the town held a memorial service for the fallen.

en mine.explanation: "En mine" means "a mine or a facial expression". When you talk about a place where coal or metal is dug out of the ground, it means "a mine": "en kulmine" (a coal mine). When you talk about a look on someone's face, it means "a facial expression": "en sur mine" (a sour look). Do not mix it up with "mine" (my). For example, "mine børn" (my children).

sentence.da: Hun lavede en sur **mine**, da hun smagte på suppen.
sentence.en: She made a sour face when she tasted the soup.

en minister.explanation: "En minister" means "a minister". To say which area a minister leads, put the area first in one word: "en sundhedsminister" (a health minister).

sentence.da: Den nye **minister** vil bygge flere skoler.
sentence.en: The new minister wants to build more schools.

en minoritet.explanation: "En minoritet" means "a minority". A common phrase is "en etnisk minoritet" (an ethnic minority).

sentence.da: Der bor en tysk **minoritet** i Sønderjylland.
sentence.en: A German minority lives in South Jutland.

en misforståelse.explanation: "En misforståelse" means "a misunderstanding". It is built from "mis-" and "en forståelse" (an understanding). The start "mis-" adds the idea of something going wrong, as in "mistillid" (distrust) and "mislykkes" (to fail).

sentence.da: Undskyld, det var bare en **misforståelse**.
sentence.en: Sorry, it was just a misunderstanding.

en mission.explanation: "En mission" means "a mission". When you talk about a goal someone feels they must reach, you can also use "mission": "Hendes mission er at redde havet" (Her mission is to save the ocean).

sentence.da: Soldaterne fik en **mission** langt bag fjendens linjer.
sentence.en: The soldiers got a mission far behind enemy lines.

en mistanke.explanation: "En mistanke" means "a suspicion". To say what you suspect, use "om" (about) after it: "Jeg har mistanke om, at han lyver" (I suspect that he is lying).

sentence.da: Politiet har en **mistanke**, men endnu ikke noget bevis.
sentence.en: The police have a suspicion, but no evidence yet.

en mobil.explanation: "En mobil" means "a mobile phone". It is the short form of "en mobiltelefon" (a mobile phone). To say you do something on your phone, use "på" (on): "Jeg ser film på mobilen" (I watch films on my phone).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dig fra min **mobil**.
sentence.en: I call you from my mobile phone.

en mobiltelefon.explanation: "En mobiltelefon" means "a mobile phone". It is built from "mobil" (mobile) and "en telefon" (a phone). The short form is "en mobil". For example, "Min mobil ligger på bordet" (My mobile phone is on the table).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til min mor på min **mobiltelefon**.
sentence.en: I call my mother on my mobile phone.

en model.explanation: "En model" means "a model". When you talk about a small copy of something, use "en model af" (a model of): "en model af et fly" (a model of a plane). When you talk about a type of product, use "en bilmodel" (a car model). When you talk about a person who shows clothes, it means a fashion model: "Hun arbejder som model" (She works as a model).

sentence.da: Min onkel bygger en **model** af et skib.
sentence.en: My uncle is building a model of a ship.

en modspiller.explanation: "En modspiller" means "an opponent (in a game)". For an opponent in a fight, an election or an argument, use "en modstander" (an opponent): "Han er min modstander i valget" (He is my opponent in the election).

sentence.da: Man kan ikke spille skak uden en **modspiller**.
sentence.en: You cannot play chess without an opponent.

en modstand.explanation: "En modstand" means "a resistance". To say people push back against something, use "at gøre modstand" (to resist): "Folk gjorde modstand mod planen" (People resisted the plan). When you talk about the force that slows a movement, use "luftmodstand" (air resistance).

sentence.da: Planen mødte stor **modstand** blandt naboerne.
sentence.en: The plan met great resistance among the neighbors.

en modstander.explanation: "En modstander" means "an opponent". To say what you are up against, use "i" (in): "Han er min modstander i valget" (He is my opponent in the election). For the person you play against in chess or tennis, use "en modspiller" (an opponent in a game): "Min modspiller i skak er min far" (My opponent in chess is my father).

sentence.da: Han er en stærk **modstander** af den nye lov.
sentence.en: He is a strong opponent of the new law.

en modsætning.explanation: "En modsætning" means "an opposite or contrast". To set two things against each other, use "i modsætning til" (unlike): "Jeg bliver hjemme, i modsætning til dig" (I am staying home, unlike you).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **modsætning** mellem rig og fattig.
sentence.en: There is a big contrast between rich and poor.

en modtagelse.explanation: "En modtagelse" means "a reception". To talk about the signal on a phone, use it like this: "Der er dårlig modtagelse her" (The reception is bad here). Do not mix it up with "en reception", which is a hotel front desk. For example, "Spørg i receptionen" (Ask at the front desk).

sentence.da: Gæsterne fik en varm **modtagelse** af værten.
sentence.en: The guests got a warm reception from the host.

en modvilje.explanation: "En modvilje" means "a reluctance". It is built from "mod" (against) and "en vilje" (a will). The same "mod" is in "modstand" (resistance), as in "at gøre modstand" (to resist).

sentence.da: Hun fortalte med **modvilje**, at hun måtte flytte.
sentence.en: She said with reluctance that she had to move.

en mole.explanation: "En mole" means "a pier". To say you walk out on one, use "på" (on): "Vi går en tur på molen" (We take a walk on the pier).

sentence.da: Der står et fyrtårn for enden af en **mole**.
sentence.en: There is a lighthouse at the end of a pier.

en moppe.explanation: "En moppe" means "a mop". The verb is "at moppe" (to mop). For example, "Jeg skal moppe gulvet" (I have to mop the floor).

sentence.da: Jeg vasker gulvet med en **moppe**.
sentence.en: I wash the floor with a mop.

en mor.explanation: "En mor" means "a mother". When you speak to your mother, use "mor" like a name: "Hej, mor!" (Hi, mom!). The "mor" in "mormor" (mother's mother) shows that the grandmother is on your mother's side.

sentence.da: Min **mor** er gift med min far.
sentence.en: My mother is married to my father.

en moral.explanation: "En moral" means "a moral or morale". When you talk about the lesson of a story, it means "a moral": "Historiens moral er, at man skal være ærlig" (The moral of the story is that you should be honest). When you talk about the mood of a team or a workplace, it means "morale": "Moralen på holdet er høj" (Team morale is high).

sentence.da: Hans **moral** siger, at man aldrig må stjæle.
sentence.en: His morals say that you must never steal.

en morbror.explanation: "En morbror" means "an uncle (mother's brother)". To talk about your father's brother, use "en farbror" (an uncle, father's brother): "Min farbror bor i Aarhus" (My uncle lives in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Min **morbror** er min mors bror og bor i Roskilde.
sentence.en: My uncle is my mother's brother and lives in Roskilde.

en morder.explanation: "En morder" means "a murderer". It is built from "et mord" (a murder). The same "mord" is in "et mordvåben" (a murder weapon).

sentence.da: Politiet leder efter en **morder**, der er flygtet.
sentence.en: The police are looking for a murderer who has escaped.

en morfar.explanation: "En morfar" means "a grandfather (mother's father)". It is built from "mor" (mother) and "far" (father). To talk about your father's father, use "en farfar" (a grandfather, father's father): "Min farfar bor på landet" (My grandfather lives in the country).

sentence.da: Min **morfar** er min mors far.
sentence.en: My grandfather is my mother's father.

en morgen.explanation: "En morgen" means "a morning". Do not mix it up with "i morgen" (tomorrow). For example, "Vi ses i morgen" (See you tomorrow). To say something happens in the morning, use "om morgenen" (in the morning): "Jeg løber om morgenen" (I run in the morning). To greet someone in the morning, say "godmorgen" (good morning): "Godmorgen, Anna!" (Good morning, Anna!).

sentence.da: Hver **morgen** spiser jeg morgenmad og drikker kaffe.
sentence.en: Every morning I eat breakfast and drink coffee.

en morgenkaffe.explanation: "En morgenkaffe" means "a morning coffee". It is built from "morgen" (morning) and "kaffe" (coffee). To say where you drink it, use "at drikke" (to drink): "Jeg drikker min morgenkaffe på altanen" (I drink my morning coffee on the balcony).

sentence.da: Min **morgenkaffe** kommer før morgenmaden.
sentence.en: My morning coffee comes before breakfast.

en morgenkåbe.explanation: "En morgenkåbe" means "a bathrobe". It is built from "morgen" (morning) and "en kåbe" (a robe). Do not mix it up with "en badekåbe", which is a robe you put on after a swim: "Jeg tager badekåben på efter svømmeturen" (I put on my robe after the swim).

sentence.da: En **morgenkåbe** tager man på, før man klæder sig på.
sentence.en: You put on a bathrobe before you get dressed.

en morgenmadsbuffet.explanation: "En morgenmadsbuffet" means "a breakfast buffet". It is built from "morgenmad" (breakfast) and "en buffet" (a buffet). To say breakfast comes with the room, use "inklusive" (including): "Prisen er inklusive morgenmad" (The price includes breakfast).

sentence.da: Ved en **morgenmadsbuffet** tager man selv, hvad man vil have.
sentence.en: At a breakfast buffet, you take whatever you want yourself.

en morgenrutine.explanation: "En morgenrutine" means "a morning routine". It is built from "morgen" (morning) and "en rutine" (a routine). To say you have one, use "at have" (to have): "Jeg har en fast morgenrutine" (I have a fixed morning routine).

sentence.da: Min **morgenrutine** er kaffe, avis og en kort gåtur.
sentence.en: My morning routine is coffee, newspaper and a short walk.

en mormor.explanation: "En mormor" means "a grandmother (mother's mother)". It is built from "mor" (mother) and "mor" (mother) again. To talk about your father's mother, use "en farmor" (a grandmother, father's mother): "Min farmor bager brød" (My grandmother bakes bread).

sentence.da: Min **mormor** er min mors mor.
sentence.en: My grandmother is my mother's mother.

en mose.explanation: "En mose" means "a bog". Do not mix it up with "mos" (moss), the small green plant. For example, "Der er mos på stenen" (There is moss on the stone).

sentence.da: Man kan synke i en **mose**, fordi jorden er våd og blød.
sentence.en: You can sink in a bog because the ground is wet and soft.

en moské.explanation: "En moské" means "a mosque". The tall tower of a mosque is "en minaret" (a minaret). To say people pray there, use "at bede" (to pray): "De beder i moskeen" (They pray in the mosque).

sentence.da: Om fredagen mødes mange muslimer i en **moské**.
sentence.en: On Fridays, many Muslims meet in a mosque.

en moster.explanation: "En moster" means "an aunt (mother's sister)". To talk about your father's sister, use "en faster" (an aunt, father's sister): "Min faster bor i Aalborg" (My aunt lives in Aalborg).

sentence.da: Min **moster** er min mors søster og bor i Odense.
sentence.en: My aunt is my mother's sister and lives in Odense.

en motor.explanation: "En motor" means "an engine". When you talk about a motor in a machine, you also use "en motor": "Plæneklipperen har en lille motor" (The lawn mower has a small motor).

sentence.da: Bådens **motor** larmer meget, når vi sejler.
sentence.en: The boat's engine is very loud when we sail.

en motorcykel.explanation: "En motorcykel" means "a motorcycle". It is built from "en motor" (an engine) and "en cykel" (a bicycle). To say you ride one, use "at køre" (to drive): "Jeg kører på motorcykel" (I ride a motorcycle). For a bicycle, use "at cykle" (to bike): "Jeg cykler på arbejde" (I bike to work).

sentence.da: Min bror kører til arbejde på en stor **motorcykel**.
sentence.en: My brother rides to work on a big motorcycle.

en motorcyklist.explanation: "En motorcyklist" means "a motorcyclist". It is built from "en motorcykel" (a motorcycle) and the ending "-ist", which names the person, as in "en cyklist" (a cyclist) and "en bilist" (a motorist).

sentence.da: En **motorcyklist** skal altid bruge hjelm.
sentence.en: A motorcyclist must always wear a helmet.

en motorvej.explanation: "En motorvej" means "a highway". It is built from "motor" (engine) and "vej" (road). When you ask for a direction, "vej" also means "way": "Hvilken vej skal vi gå?" (Which way should we go?)

sentence.da: Vi skal køre på **motorvej** i to timer.
sentence.en: We have to drive on the highway for two hours.

en muffin.explanation: "En muffin" means "a muffin". To name the flavor, put it first: "en blåbærmuffin" (a blueberry muffin).

sentence.da: Man bager en **muffin** af mel, sukker og æg.
sentence.en: You bake a muffin from flour, sugar and eggs.

en muffinform.explanation: "En muffinform" means "a muffin tin". It is built from "en muffin" (a muffin) and "en form" (a baking mold).

sentence.da: Hun hælder dejen i en **muffinform**.
sentence.en: She pours the batter into a muffin tin.

en muldvarp.explanation: "En muldvarp" means "a mole", the animal. When you talk about a person who secretly works for the other side from inside a group, it also means "a mole": "Han var en muldvarp i firmaet" (He was a mole in the company).

sentence.da: En **muldvarp** bor under jorden og ser næsten ingenting.
sentence.en: A mole lives under the ground and sees almost nothing.

en mulepose.explanation: "En mulepose" means "a tote bag". To say you have your own bag with you at the shop, use "at have med" (to have along): "Jeg har min mulepose med" (I have my tote bag with me).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger varerne i min **mulepose**, så jeg slipper for plastik.
sentence.en: I put the groceries in my tote bag, so I avoid plastic.

en mulighed.explanation: "En mulighed" means "a possibility". When you count your choices, it means "an option": "Vi har to muligheder" (We have two options). When you talk about a chance that comes along, it means "an opportunity": "Jeg fik muligheden for at rejse" (I got the opportunity to travel).

sentence.da: Det er den eneste **mulighed**, vi har.
sentence.en: It is the only option we have.

en mund.explanation: "En mund" means "a mouth". To tell someone to open their mouth, say: "Åbn munden" (Open your mouth). To tell someone to be quiet, "Hold munden!" means "Shut up!", and it is rude.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser og taler med min **mund**.
sentence.en: I eat and talk with my mouth.

en munk.explanation: "En munk" means "a monk". To say what someone became, leave out "en": "Han blev munk" (He became a monk).

sentence.da: En **munk** bor i et kloster og beder hver dag.
sentence.en: A monk lives in a monastery and prays every day.

en mur.explanation: "En mur" means "a wall". When you talk about a wall around a garden or on a house, use "mur": "en mur om haven" (a wall around the garden). When you talk about a wall inside a room, use "en væg" (a wall): "Billedet hænger på væggen" (The picture hangs on the wall).

sentence.da: Byen har en gammel **mur** af sten.
sentence.en: The town has an old wall of stone.

en murer.explanation: "En murer" means "a bricklayer". It comes from "en mur" (a wall). The same "mur" is in "en mursten" (a brick).

sentence.da: En **murer** lægger sten på sten, indtil væggen er færdig.
sentence.en: A bricklayer lays stone on stone until the wall is finished.

en mursten.explanation: "En mursten" means "a brick". It is built from "en mur" (a wall) and "en sten" (a stone). To say a house is made of brick, use "af" (of): "Huset er bygget af mursten" (The house is built of brick).

sentence.da: En **mursten** er ofte rød og lavet af ler.
sentence.en: A brick is often red and made of clay.

en mus.explanation: "En mus" means "a mouse", the animal. When you talk about the device you click with on a computer, use "en computermus" (a computer mouse).

sentence.da: En **mus** er lille og spiser ost.
sentence.en: A mouse is small and eats cheese.

en musiker.explanation: "En musiker" means "a musician". It comes from "musik" (music). To say a musician plays in a group, use "at spille i" (to play in): "Hun spiller i et orkester" (She plays in an orchestra).

sentence.da: Min onkel er **musiker** og spiller i et band.
sentence.en: My uncle is a musician and plays in a band.

en musikfestival.explanation: "En musikfestival" means "a music festival". It is built from "musik" (music) and "festival" (festival). The same "musik" is in "en musiker" (a musician).

sentence.da: Hver sommer hører vi mange bands på en **musikfestival**.
sentence.en: Every summer we hear many bands at a music festival.

en muskel.explanation: "En muskel" means "a muscle". To say your muscles are sore, say: "Jeg har ondt i musklerne" (My muscles hurt).

sentence.da: Du bruger en **muskel**, når du løfter armen.
sentence.en: You use a muscle when you lift your arm.

en musling.explanation: "En musling" means "a mussel or clam". To name the kind, put it first: "en blåmusling" (a blue mussel).

sentence.da: Hun åbner en **musling** og finder en perle.
sentence.en: She opens a mussel and finds a pearl.

en muslingeskal.explanation: "En muslingeskal" means "a seashell". It is built from "en musling" (a mussel / clam) and "en skal" (a shell). The shell of a snail is "en snegleskal". For example, "Sneglen kravler ind i snegleskallen" (The snail crawls into its shell).

sentence.da: En **muslingeskal** beskytter dyret, der bor inde i den.
sentence.en: A seashell protects the animal that lives inside it.

en myg.explanation: "En myg" means "a mosquito". To name the bite, add "stik" (sting): "et myggestik" (a mosquito bite).

sentence.da: En **myg** stak mig i armen i nat.
sentence.en: A mosquito bit me on the arm last night.

en myndighed.explanation: "En myndighed" means "an authority". To talk about the authorities as a group, use "myndighederne" (the authorities): "Myndighederne har lukket vejen" (The authorities have closed the road).

sentence.da: Skattevæsenet er en **myndighed**, som opkræver skat.
sentence.en: The tax office is an authority that collects tax.

en myre.explanation: "En myre" means "an ant". To say ants are somewhere, use "der er" (there are): "Der er myrer i køkkenet" (There are ants in the kitchen).

sentence.da: En **myre** er lille og bærer mad hjem.
sentence.en: An ant is small and carries food home.

en myretue.explanation: "En myretue" means "an anthill". It is built from "en myre" (an ant) and "en tue" (a small mound). To warn someone, say: "Pas på, du træder ikke på myretuen" (Careful, do not step on the anthill).

sentence.da: Tusindvis af myrer bor i en **myretue**.
sentence.en: Thousands of ants live in an anthill.

en myte.explanation: "En myte" means "a myth". When you talk about a belief that is common but not true, use it too: "Det er en myte, at man kun bruger ti procent af hjernen" (It is a myth that people only use ten percent of the brain).

sentence.da: Fortællingen om Thor og hans hammer er en gammel **myte**.
sentence.en: The tale of Thor and his hammer is an old myth.

en måde.explanation: "En måde" means "a way or manner". To say "in that way", use "på den måde": "Jeg gør det på den måde" (I do it that way). To say "somehow", use "på en eller anden måde": "Jeg klarer det på en eller anden måde" (I will manage it somehow). For a road or a direction, use "en vej" (a road, a way): "Hvilken vej skal vi gå?" (Which way should we go?)

sentence.da: Det er en god **måde** at lære på.
sentence.en: That is a good way to learn.

en måge.explanation: "En måge" means "a seagull". To name a kind, put it first: "en hættemåge" (a black-headed gull).

sentence.da: En **måge** flyver over havet og leder efter fisk.
sentence.en: A seagull flies over the sea looking for fish.

en måler.explanation: "En måler" means "a meter or gauge". It comes from "at måle" (to measure). To say what a meter measures, put the thing first: "en elmåler" (an electricity meter) and "en vandmåler" (a water meter).

sentence.da: En **måler** viser, hvor meget strøm vi bruger hjemme.
sentence.en: A meter shows how much electricity we use at home.

en målgruppe.explanation: "En målgruppe" means "a target group". It is built from "et mål" (a goal) and "en gruppe" (a group). To say who a product is for, use "som" (as): "Unge er vores målgruppe" (Young people are our target group).

sentence.da: Børnebøger har børn og forældre som **målgruppe**.
sentence.en: Children's books have children and parents as the target group.

en måling.explanation: "En måling" means "a measurement". To name an opinion poll, put "mening" (opinion) first: "en meningsmåling" (an opinion poll). Do not mix it up with "maling" (paint), which has a plain "a" instead of "å". For example, "Jeg køber maling til væggen" (I am buying paint for the wall).

sentence.da: En **måling** af rummet viste, at det er fire meter langt.
sentence.en: A measurement of the room showed that it is four meters long.

en målmand.explanation: "En målmand" means "a goalkeeper". It is built from "et mål" (a goal) and "en mand" (a man). The same "mål" also means an aim in life. For example, "Mit mål er at lære dansk" (My goal is to learn Danish).

sentence.da: Han vil være **målmand**, fordi han griber bolden godt.
sentence.en: He wants to be a goalkeeper because he catches the ball well.

en måne.explanation: "En måne" means "a moon". To say the moon is shining, use "måne" with the ending "-n": "Månen skinner i nat" (The moon shines tonight). Do not mix it up with "en måned" (a month). For example, "Der er tolv måneder i et år" (There are twelve months in a year).

sentence.da: En **måne** går rundt om en planet.
sentence.en: A moon goes around a planet.

en måned.explanation: "En måned" means "a month". To say how much you pay each month, use "om måneden" (per month): "Jeg betaler tusind kroner om måneden" (I pay a thousand kroner a month).

sentence.da: Der er cirka tredive dage i en **måned**.
sentence.en: There are about thirty days in a month.

sentence.da: En **mår** er et slankt rovdyr og klatrer godt.
sentence.en: A marten is a slim predator and climbs well.

en mælkebøtte.explanation: "En mælkebøtte" means "a dandelion". Literally, it is a "milk bucket": it is built from "mælk" (milk) and "en bøtte" (a bucket).

sentence.da: En **mælkebøtte** er gul, men bliver senere hvid og luftig.
sentence.en: A dandelion is yellow, but later becomes white and fluffy.

en mængde.explanation: "En mængde" means "an amount". To say a large amount of something you cannot count, use "en stor mængde" (a large amount): "en stor mængde vand" (a large amount of water). For things you can count, use "et antal" (a number): "et antal bøger" (a number of books).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge en lille **mængde** salt.
sentence.en: You need a small amount of salt.

en møbelforretning.explanation: "En møbelforretning" means "a furniture store". It is built from "et møbel" (a piece of furniture) and "en forretning" (a shop). The word "forretning" also means "a business deal". For example, "at gøre en god forretning" (to make a good deal).

sentence.da: I en **møbelforretning** kan man købe sofaer og borde.
sentence.en: In a furniture store you can buy sofas and tables.

en mølle.explanation: "En mølle" means "a mill", as in a flour mill. To name the kind of mill, put it first: "en vindmølle" (a windmill).

sentence.da: Bageren køber mel fra den gamle **mølle**.
sentence.en: The baker buys flour from the old mill.

en mønt.explanation: "En mønt" means "a coin". For paper money, use "en seddel" (a banknote): "Jeg har en seddel på hundrede kroner" (I have a banknote worth a hundred kroner).

sentence.da: En **mønt** er rund og lavet af metal.
sentence.en: A coin is round and made of metal.

et madbud.explanation: "Et madbud" means "a food delivery person". It is built from "mad" (food) and "et bud" (a messenger). To say you have food brought to your home, use "at bestille" (to order): "Jeg bestiller mad hjem" (I order food to be delivered).

sentence.da: Et **madbud** kommer med maden hjem til døren.
sentence.en: A food delivery person brings the food home to the door.

et magasin.explanation: "Et magasin" means "a magazine". Another word for a magazine is "et blad". For example, "Jeg læser et blad" (I read a magazine).

sentence.da: Jeg læser et **magasin** i venteværelset.
sentence.en: I read a magazine in the waiting room.

et maleri.explanation: "Et maleri" means "a painting". It comes from the verb "at male" (to paint). The person who paints pictures is "en maler" (a painter).

sentence.da: Der hænger et flot **maleri** over sofaen.
sentence.en: A beautiful painting hangs over the sofa.

et mandskab.explanation: "Et mandskab" means "a crew". To talk about one person in the crew, say "et medlem af mandskabet" (a member of the crew).

sentence.da: Skibet har et **mandskab** på tyve personer.
sentence.en: The ship has a crew of twenty people.

et manuskript.explanation: "Et manuskript" means "a manuscript or script". When you talk about a text before it is printed, it means "a manuscript": "Han sender sit manuskript til forlaget" (He sends his manuscript to the publisher). When you talk about the written text of a film or a play, it means "a script": "Skuespilleren læser manuskriptet" (The actor reads the script).

sentence.da: Skuespillerne har lært deres **manuskript** udenad før premieren.
sentence.en: The actors have learned their script by heart before the premiere.

et maraton.explanation: "Et maraton" means "a marathon". To say you will run one, use "at løbe" (to run): "Jeg skal løbe et maraton i oktober" (I am going to run a marathon in October).

sentence.da: Hun træner hårdt til sit første **maraton**.
sentence.en: She is training hard for her first marathon.

et mareridt.explanation: "Et mareridt" means "a nightmare". When you talk about a terrible situation, you can also use "mareridt": "Trafikken var et mareridt" (The traffic was a nightmare).

sentence.da: Jeg havde et forfærdeligt **mareridt** i nat.
sentence.en: I had a terrible nightmare last night.

et marked.explanation: "Et marked" means "a market". To name the kind, put it first: "et loppemarked" (a flea market). When you talk about the economy, "markedet" means the market for a product: "Markedet for elbiler vokser" (The market for electric cars is growing).

sentence.da: Vi køber frugt og grøntsager på et **marked**.
sentence.en: We buy fruit and vegetables at a market.

et marsvin.explanation: "Et marsvin" means "a guinea pig or porpoise". When you talk about the small furry pet, it means "a guinea pig": "Vores marsvin bor i et bur" (Our guinea pig lives in a cage). When you talk about the small sea mammal, it means "a porpoise": "Marsvinet svømmer i havet" (The porpoise swims in the sea).

sentence.da: Vores **marsvin** elsker gulerødder og bor i et bur.
sentence.en: Our guinea pig loves carrots and lives in a cage.

et materiale.explanation: "Et materiale" means "a material". When you talk about information or study material, use it too: "Jeg læser materialet" (I read the material).

sentence.da: Stål er et stærkt **materiale**.
sentence.en: Steel is a strong material.

et medicinskab.explanation: "Et medicinskab" means "a medicine cabinet". It is built from "medicin" (medicine) and "et skab" (a cabinet). The same "skab" is in "et køleskab" (a refrigerator) and "et klædeskab" (a wardrobe).

sentence.da: Pillerne ligger i et lille **medicinskab** på badeværelset.
sentence.en: The pills are in a small medicine cabinet in the bathroom.

et medie.explanation: "Et medie" means "a medium". To talk about the press, TV and radio together, use the plural form "medierne" (the media): "Medierne skriver om sagen" (The media write about the case).

sentence.da: Radioen er et **medie**, som formidler nyheder og musik.
sentence.en: The radio is a medium that spreads news and music.

et medlem.explanation: "Et medlem" means "a member". The ending "-skab" turns it into "et medlemskab" (a membership). For example, "Mit medlemskab koster to hundrede kroner om året" (My membership costs two hundred kroner a year).

sentence.da: Min bror er **medlem** af en fodboldklub.
sentence.en: My brother is a member of a soccer club.

et medlemskab.explanation: "Et medlemskab" means "a membership". It is built from "et medlem" (a member) and the ending "-skab". The same ending makes "et venskab" (a friendship) from "en ven" (a friend).

sentence.da: Et **medlemskab** i klubben koster hundrede kroner om måneden.
sentence.en: A membership in the club costs a hundred kroner a month.

et mellemnavn.explanation: "Et mellemnavn" means "a middle name". It is built from "mellem" (between) and "et navn" (a name). The word "mellem" also starts "et mellemmåltid" (a snack between meals).

sentence.da: Marie er mit **mellemnavn**.
sentence.en: Marie is my middle name.

et menneske.explanation: "Et menneske" means "a human being". To talk about people in general, use the plural "mennesker": "Der er mange mennesker i byen" (There are many people in the town).

sentence.da: Du er et **menneske**, ikke et dyr.
sentence.en: You are a human being, not an animal.

et menukort.explanation: "Et menukort" means "a menu". To ask a waiter for the menu, say: "Må jeg se menukortet?" (May I see the menu?). To talk about a set meal with several courses, use "en menu": "Vi bestiller en menu med tre retter" (We order a set meal with three courses).

sentence.da: Vi ser på et **menukort** i restauranten.
sentence.en: We look at a menu in the restaurant.

et mesterskab.explanation: "Et mesterskab" means "a championship". It is built from "en mester" (a master) and the ending "-skab". To name a world championship, use the short form "VM" (verdensmesterskab): "Hun vandt VM i svømning" (She won the World Championship in swimming).

sentence.da: Vinderen af et **mesterskab** får en guldmedalje.
sentence.en: The winner of a championship gets a gold medal.

et metal.explanation: "Et metal" means "a metal". To talk about the music style, use "metal" without an article: "Jeg lytter til metal" (I listen to metal).

sentence.da: Aluminium er et let **metal**.
sentence.en: Aluminum is a light metal.

et middagsselskab.explanation: "Et middagsselskab" means "a dinner party". It is built from "middag" (dinner) and "et selskab" (a party). The word "selskab" also means a company, as in "et forsikringsselskab" (an insurance company).

sentence.da: Vi har inviteret venner til et **middagsselskab** på lørdag.
sentence.en: We have invited friends to a dinner party on Saturday.

et middel.explanation: "Et middel" means "a means or remedy". To say what a remedy works against, add "mod" (against): "et middel mod hovedpine" (a remedy for headaches). To talk about money, use the plural "midler" (funds): "offentlige midler" (public funds).

sentence.da: Motion er et godt **middel** mod stress.
sentence.en: Exercise is a good remedy for stress.

et militær.explanation: "Et militær" means "a military". To describe something as military, use the adjective "militær": "et militært køretøj" (a military vehicle).

sentence.da: Landets **militær** har både soldater og skibe.
sentence.en: The country's military has both soldiers and ships.

et miljø.explanation: "Et miljø" means "an environment". To talk about the conditions at a workplace, use "et arbejdsmiljø" (a work environment): "Vi har et godt arbejdsmiljø" (We have a good work environment).

sentence.da: Plastik i havet er dårligt for vores **miljø**.
sentence.en: Plastic in the sea is bad for our environment.

et mindretal.explanation: "Et mindretal" means "a minority". It is built from "mindre" (less) and "et tal" (a number).

sentence.da: Kun et **mindretal** stemte for forslaget, så det faldt.
sentence.en: Only a minority voted for the proposal, so it failed.

et ministerium.explanation: "Et ministerium" means "a ministry". To name a ministry, put its subject in front of "ministeriet" (the ministry): "Finansministeriet" (the Ministry of Finance).

sentence.da: Skatteministeriet er et **ministerium**, der styrer skatten i landet.
sentence.en: The Ministry of Taxation is a ministry that manages taxes in the country.

et minut.explanation: "Et minut" means "a minute". To ask someone to wait a short while, say: "Vent et minut" (Wait a minute).

sentence.da: Et **minut** er tres sekunder.
sentence.en: A minute is sixty seconds.

et mirakel.explanation: "Et mirakel" means "a miracle". To describe something as miraculous, use the adjective "mirakuløs": "en mirakuløs redning" (a miraculous rescue).

sentence.da: Det er et **mirakel**, at han overlevede ulykken uden skader.
sentence.en: It is a miracle that he survived the accident without injuries.

et missil.explanation: "Et missil" means "a missile". To talk about a rocket for fireworks or space, use "en raket" (a rocket): "Vi skyder en raket op ved midnat" (We shoot a rocket up at midnight).

sentence.da: Et **missil** ramte en bygning i nat.
sentence.en: A missile hit a building last night.

et modermærke.explanation: "Et modermærke" means "a mole", as in a spot on the skin. It is built from "moder" (mother) and "et mærke" (a mark). To talk about the animal, use "en muldvarp": "En muldvarp graver i haven" (A mole digs in the garden).

sentence.da: Lægen kigger på det mørke **modermærke** på min ryg.
sentence.en: The doctor looks at the dark mole on my back.

et modersmål.explanation: "Et modersmål" means "a mother tongue". It is built from "moder" (mother) and "mål" (speech).

sentence.da: Mit **modersmål** er engelsk, men jeg lærer dansk.
sentence.en: My mother tongue is English, but I am learning Danish.

et modeshow.explanation: "Et modeshow" means "a fashion show". It is built from "mode" (fashion) and the English word "show". The word "mode" also starts "et modemagasin" (a fashion magazine).

sentence.da: Til et **modeshow** går modeller rundt i nyt tøj.
sentence.en: At a fashion show, models walk around in new clothes.

et modsætningsord.explanation: "Et modsætningsord" means "an antonym". It is built from "en modsætning" (an opposite) and "et ord" (a word). To ask for the opposite of a word, say: "Hvad er modsætningsordet til stor?" (What is the antonym of big?).

sentence.da: Varm er et **modsætningsord** til kold.
sentence.en: Warm is an antonym of cold.

et molekyle.explanation: "Et molekyle" means "a molecule". To name the molecule of a substance, put the substance in front: "et vandmolekyle" (a water molecule).

sentence.da: Hvert **molekyle** i vand har to brintatomer og ét iltatom.
sentence.en: Each molecule in water has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

et monster.explanation: "Et monster" means "a monster". Do not mix it up with "et mønster" (a pattern). To talk about a pattern on clothes, say: "et mønster på tøjet" (a pattern on the clothes).

sentence.da: Barnet er bange for et **monster** under sengen.
sentence.en: The child is afraid of a monster under the bed.

et monument.explanation: "Et monument" means "a monument". To say who or what a monument honors, add "for": "et monument for kongen" (a monument for the king). To say people build one, use "at rejse" (to put up): "De rejser et monument" (They put up a monument).

sentence.da: Det store **monument** minder om krigen.
sentence.en: The big monument is a reminder of the war.

et mord.explanation: "Et mord" means "a murder". To say someone commits murder, use the verb "at begå" (to commit): "at begå mord" (to commit murder).

sentence.da: Politiet undersøger det **mord**, der skete i går.
sentence.en: The police are investigating the murder that happened yesterday.

et motel.explanation: "Et motel" means "a motel". The plural ends in "-ler", not "-s". For example, "Der er to moteller i byen" (There are two motels in the town).

sentence.da: Vi sover på et **motel** ved motorvejen.
sentence.en: We are sleeping at a motel by the highway.

et motiv.explanation: "Et motiv" means "a motive or subject". To say what a photo or painting shows, use "motiv" for its subject: "Motivet på billedet er en kirke" (The subject of the picture is a church).

sentence.da: Politiet leder stadig efter et **motiv** for forbrydelsen.
sentence.en: The police are still looking for a motive for the crime.

et museum.explanation: "Et museum" means "a museum". To say you are at the museum, use "på" (at): "Jeg er på museet" (I am at the museum).

sentence.da: Vi ser gamle ting på et **museum**.
sentence.en: We see old things at a museum.

et mysterium.explanation: "Et mysterium" means "a mystery". To say someone solves a mystery, use "at løse" (to solve): "Detektiven løser mysteriet" (The detective solves the mystery).

sentence.da: Hvordan pyramiderne blev bygget, er stadig et **mysterium**.
sentence.en: How the pyramids were built is still a mystery.

et mål.explanation: "Et mål" means "a goal". To say someone scored in a sport, say: "Han scorede to mål" (He scored two goals).

sentence.da: Mit **mål** er at tale godt dansk.
sentence.en: My goal is to speak good Danish.

et målebånd.explanation: "Et målebånd" means "a tape measure". It is built from "at måle" (to measure) and "et bånd" (a band). The word "måle" also starts "et målebæger" (a measuring cup).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **målebånd**, når jeg køber møbler.
sentence.en: I use a tape measure when I buy furniture.

et målebæger.explanation: "Et målebæger" means "a measuring cup". It is built from "at måle" (to measure) and "et bæger" (a cup). The word "måle" also starts "et målebånd" (a tape measure).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **målebæger** til at måle sukker.
sentence.en: I use a measuring cup to measure sugar.

et måltid.explanation: "Et måltid" means "a meal". To say a meal is hot, use "varmt" (hot): "Vi spiser et varmt måltid hver aften" (We eat a hot meal every evening). To talk about the food itself, use "mad" (food): "Maden er god" (The food is good).

sentence.da: Dagens vigtigste **måltid** er morgenmad.
sentence.en: The most important meal of the day is breakfast.

et månedskort.explanation: "Et månedskort" means "a monthly pass". It is built from "måned" (month) and "kort" (card). The word "kort" also means a card in "et kreditkort" (a credit card).

sentence.da: Med et **månedskort** kan jeg tage bussen hver dag.
sentence.en: With a monthly pass, I can take the bus every day.

et mærke.explanation: "Et mærke" means "a brand or mark". To ask what brand something is, say: "Hvilket mærke er din telefon?" (What brand is your phone?). To talk about a mark on a surface, say: "et mærke på væggen" (a mark on the wall).

sentence.da: Det er et dyrt **mærke**, men jakken er flot.
sentence.en: It is an expensive brand, but the jacket is nice.

et møbel.explanation: "Et møbel" means "a piece of furniture". To talk about all your furniture together, use the plural "møbler" (furniture): "Vi køber nye møbler" (We are buying new furniture).

sentence.da: En sofa er et **møbel**.
sentence.en: A sofa is a piece of furniture.
